previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A woman with end-stage renal disease on hemodialysis was admitted with chest pain and hyperkalemia. Initial evaluation revealed fluid overload and elevated potassium, managed with medical therapy and dialysis. Her left arm arteriovenous fistula, previously complicated by steal syndrome, was evaluated with a fistulogram, which revealed stenosis. During attempted angioplasty, the fistula ruptured, causing a hematoma that required surgical evacuation. The fistula was rendered nonfunctional, and a temporary right subclavian dialysis line was placed, later converted to a tunneled catheter. Her chest pain resolved, potassium normalized, and INR stabilized after warfarin adjustment. She was discharged home with instructions to protect her right arm for future fistula creation, continue medications, monitor weight, and follow up with transplant surgery and nephrology.

Discharge Instructions:
Dear ___,

___ was a pleasure taking care of you during your stay at ___. 
You were admitted for treatment of your calciphylaxis, which 
involved dialysis with sodium thiosulfate and oral medications. 
Eventually it was decided that removal of most of your 
parathyroid gland would help calcium balance in your body. 
Afterwards, your bones, which had been breaking down their 
calcium for a long time, suddenly became hungry for it back. 
This required regular checks of your calcium and medication to 
keep your calcium level up. Overtime, your calcium levels 
continued to improve, however still requires daily IV 
medications to keep it elevated.

Given that your calcium level was low, the decision was made to 
not do IV sodium thiosulfate to treat your calciphylaxis since 
this drug would further decrease your calcium level. However, 
after speaking with dermatolgy, the decision was made to do 
intralesional sodium thiosulfate. With these injections, your 
calciphylaxis lesions improved.

One of the major issues for you was pain in your right leg. 
While calciphylaxis was a major component of your leg pain, it 
was also determined that your blood flow to your right foot was 
poor, and your toes were becoming painful and darker due to 
decreased blood flow. On ___ your vascular cardiologist 
performed angiography and an atherectomy to help restore blood 
flow to your foot. While part of this was successful, the 
procedure was complicated by bits of the plaque flowing 
downstream and disrupting the blood flow to your feet. You were 
giving lots of pain medication to help with the pain in your 
legs.

 

Weigh yourself every morning, call MD if weight goes up more 
than 3 lbs.

Wishing you well,
Your ___ Medicine Team
